home.heroText: Karahan brings the cooking of the Silk Road to Winterthur: laghman from freshly pulled dough, polo from the kazan, kebab over charcoal. All halal, all by hand.
home.firstTimeText: Uyghur cuisine sits between Central Asia and China: dough, lamb, spices and plenty of fresh vegetables. If it is new to you, order these three. Together they tell the whole story.

1.title: Laghman
1.text: Hand-pulled noodles with lamb and vegetables. The dish a Uyghur kitchen is judged by.

2.title: Polo
2.text: Rice, lamb, carrots. Looks simple, takes hours. Sweet, salty, deep.

3.title: Shish kebab
3.text: Lamb over charcoal, cumin, chili. Comes straight from the grill to your table.

home.craftTitle: What you see is being made right now
home.craftText: Our dough is kneaded in the morning and rests until it is pulled. Manti and chüchüre are folded one by one by hand. The kebab never waits: it goes from grill to table.

craftPoints.1: Dough fresh daily, noodles pulled to order
craftPoints.2: Lamb and chicken from halal-certified sources
craftPoints.3: Spices from Kashgar: cumin, chili, saffron

home.cultureTitle: A piece of Kashgar in Winterthur
home.cultureText: The ikat fabrics on the columns, the doppa hats, the pictures of Ürümqi, Turpan and the Heytgah mosque: everything at Karahan speaks of where our food comes from. In Uyghur culture a guest is never just a customer. Whoever sits down gets tea first.
home.sharingText: Dapanji, mixed grill, göshnan: some dishes are made for the middle of the table. For families, friends, teams.
home.visitText: A few minutes from Winterthur main station. Parking nearby.

home.instagramText: New glimpses every day on Instagram and TikTok.
home.bookBannerText: Online in under a minute. Confirmation by email, free cancellation up to two hours before.

about.title: About us
about.lead: Karahan is a Uyghur restaurant in Winterthur. We cook what we cooked at home: dough, lamb, vegetables, spices and tea. Not simplified, not adapted.
about.whyText1: The Uyghurs have lived along the Silk Road for centuries, between Central Asia and China. Their food carries both: pulled noodles and wok from the east, pilaf, kebab and dumplings from the west. Halal, spiced, full of vegetables.
about.whyText2: In Switzerland this cuisine is almost nowhere to be found. We opened Karahan to change that. The name goes back to the Karakhanids, who ruled from Kashgar in the 10th century.

1.title: Dough is the main event
1.text: Laghman is pulled, not cut. Manti and chüchüre are folded, samsa and göshnan baked. All made fresh every day.

2.title: Lamb, cumin, chili
2.text: The base spices at the grill. Star anise, coriander and saffron in teas and soups.

3.title: Everything is halal
3.text: Meat from halal-certified sources, no pork, no alcohol in the food.

4.title: Eating together
4.text: Big plates go in the middle. Tea comes first. Whoever sits with us is a guest, not a customer.

kashgar.title: Kashgar
kashgar.text: The old oasis city on the western edge of the Taklamakan. The Heytgah mosque, the Sunday market, the tea houses. This is where our laghman comes from.

urumqi.title: Ürümqi
urumqi.text: The capital, set against the Tianshan mountains. Big kitchens, big plates. Dapanji is its best-known dish.

turpan.title: Turpan
turpan.text: The lowest and hottest oasis. Grapes, raisins, melons. The raisins in our polo are a nod to it.
